_doc: The marks agent products draw on a page while they work, which cake.js watches so that cake knows when each was there (plan steps S3.3, S3.7; GOAL A5: where a human took over; docs/collect-format.md, records 'marker' and 'markers'). build_js.py puts the 'page' object into cake.js as CFG.markers: how often to look, the shape of an extension's closed-shadow-root host, and per mark either element ids and a CSS selector (the mark is an element of the page's own DOM: it appeared or went away; ids are looked up directly, the selector is matched again only after the page's DOM changed: 'attributes' lists every attribute a selector reads, so that a change of one counts) or spots to hit-test (the mark is drawn inside a closed shadow root, which no selector reaches: document.elementFromPoint at a spot returns the host while the mark covers it; spots are tested only while <body> or <html> has a child of the host's shape). A spot is x, a fraction of the viewport's width, and top or bottom, CSS px from that edge. 'markers' says what each mark is: the product (the id the lists and env_rules.json name it by where the lists have it, else a short name of our own), its kind (legend), the product versions and the date of the evidence, its grade (env_rules.json's legend; only 'measured' has been seen in our own recordings: re-grade a mark once the user's recordings show it), its sources (source_refs), known collisions, and the words a reason uses ({span}, written as 'spans' says, times from the visit's start). 'turn_kinds': the kinds whose spans bound the agent's turn, which the behaviour timeline gives to the agent (agentcake/detect/timeline.py). 'recorder': the mark that the recorder's own check of the indicator (its raw.js 'overlay' items) stands for, so that its recordings are read like cake.js's (env_signals.from_lab). Products redraw their marks with new versions, so this file is updated on its own: edit it, then run python3 -I agentcake/build_js.py. Selectors copied from agent-detector (MIT) and botscent (MIT) are credited in source_refs and THIRD_PARTY.md.

kinds.indicator: Shown while the agent works and taken away when it stops: its times bound the agent's turn.
kinds.waiting: Shown while the agent waits for the human: its turn is paused.
kinds.attached: Shown while the product holds the tab, working or not.
kinds.action: Shown for a moment around each action.
kinds.residue: Put on the page once and left there: when it appeared, not when the agent stopped.

source_refs.claude-chrome-1.0.107: Claude in Chrome 1.0.107 as installed (extension fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn), assets/agent-visual-indicator.js, read on 2026-11-13 (not run, not changed)
source_refs.lab: Agent Cake's lab recordings of 2026-11-11 (ours): Claude in Chrome 1.0.106 driven by Claude Code, 4 sessions
source_refs.agent-detector: doubleagent-so/agent-detector 0.4.1, commit a523214c3b6740a96c312dd011f8b2310589879a, MIT: src/catalog/fingerprinted.ts (the selectors) and src/catalog/entries.ts (where each comes from)
source_refs.botscent: nalinbhardwaj/botscent 1.2.0, commit 7f948003, MIT: src/page/observe.ts (markers) and registry/reasons.json
source_refs.cheq: CHEQ, 'The Cyborg Session: reversing and detecting the Claude AI agent Chrome extension', 2026-02-18, updated 2026-05-29 (a detection vendor's research)
source_refs.recorder: The data-collection kit's recorder (not part of Agent Cake), static/raw.js: its `overlay` items, as of 2026-11-13

claude-chrome.working.evidence: 1.0.107's agent-visual-indicator.js: the 'Claude is working here' tag (#claude-page-tag, data-state working), 47 px high, centred at the top edge or, when the agent's next target is under it, at the bottom edge; pointer-events auto; inside the host's closed shadow root. It is shown while the agent works and removed when it stops; for a screenshot it is made transparent, not removed, so that it stays in elementFromPoint. Lab 2026-11-11 (1.0.106): the host, an attribute-less <div> with display: contents under <body>, on 13 of 13 pages. Not yet in a recording of 1.0.107: re-grade after the hand-off recordings (handoff-cic).
claude-chrome.working.collisions: Another extension that draws a clickable mark at the same spot from an attribute-less display: contents host (none known; untested). While the page is hidden the extension draws nothing, and cake.js does not look.

claude-chrome.waiting.evidence: 1.0.107's agent-visual-indicator.js: the 'Claude needs your input' tag (#claude-page-tag-rest, data-state waiting), 44 px high, 20 px from the top edge (or the bottom edge), centred. The spot, 56 px from the top, is below the working tag (47 px), so only this tag covers it.
claude-chrome.waiting.collisions: At the bottom edge the tag covers the spot of claude-chrome.bottom instead, and this spot sees nothing.
claude-chrome.waiting.text: Claude in Chrome was waiting for human input {span}
claude-chrome.waiting.detail: Its waiting indicator was on screen {span}.

claude-chrome.bottom.evidence: 1.0.107's agent-visual-indicator.js: three marks cover this spot, 52 px from the bottom edge: the Stop button (#claude-agent-stop-container, about 42 px high, 16 px from the bottom; shown while the agent works without the page tag), the tab's pill (#claude-static-indicator-container, the same place, shown while the tab is shared with Claude, working or not) and the 'needs your input' tag at the bottom edge (20 to 64 px). The working tag at the bottom edge (0 to 47 px) stays below the spot. The recorder (its raw.js) hit-tests 36 px from the bottom instead, which the working tag covers too.
claude-chrome.bottom.collisions: Which of the three marks it was is not known.
claude-chrome.bottom.text: Claude in Chrome showed its tab controls {span}
claude-chrome.bottom.detail: Its stop button or tab pill was on screen {span}.

claude-chrome.page-dom.evidence: botscent's claude.marker.active: these ids are on the page while the agent acts and gone before the human's first click (measured by botscent on 2026-10-02). From 1.0.105 the extension draws them inside its closed shadow root: lab 2026-11-11, 0 of 4 sessions of 1.0.106.
claude-chrome.page-dom.collisions: A site's own element with one of these ids.
claude-chrome.page-dom.detail: Its indicator from an older version was on the page {span}.

claude-chrome.styles.evidence: CHEQ: the extension adds this <style> element with its stop container, and it stays after the agent stops; agent-detector counts it as weaker evidence than the indicator.
claude-chrome.styles.collisions: A site's own element with this id.
claude-chrome.styles.text: Page styling from an older version of Claude in Chrome was present {span}
claude-chrome.styles.detail: Its style sheet from an older version was on the page {span}.

comet.overlay.evidence: agent-detector's catalogue (#pplx-agent-overlay-stop-button, and any id starting with pplx-agent, which the selector covers; it cites Castle's research and the MIT AI Agent Index); research note 20 lists the stop button among Comet's traces. Not measured by us.
comet.overlay.collisions: A site's own element whose id starts with pplx-agent.
comet.overlay.detail: Comet's agent overlay was on the page {span}.

chatgpt-chrome.badge.evidence: botscent's chatgpt.badge.active: ChatGPT for Chrome badges the page's icon while it works (71 samples in 17 documents, botscent's measurement). Not measured by us.
chatgpt-chrome.badge.detail: Its activity badge was on the page's icon {span}.

fellou.highlight.detail: Fellou's highlight was on the page {span}.

claude-chrome.recorder.evidence: The recorder's raw.js hit-tests the middle of the viewport 12 px from the top and 12 px and 36 px from the bottom every 250 ms and counts a hit on an attribute-less <div> under <body>: 1.0.107's working tag at either edge (claude-chrome.working) and, 36 px from the bottom, also its Stop button, the tab pill and the 'needs your input' tag at the bottom edge (part of claude-chrome.bottom). Only in the recorder's recordings; cake.js watches the marks of 'page'.
claude-chrome.recorder.collisions: The tab pill shows while the tab is shared with Claude, working or not, and the 'needs your input' tag while it waits for the human: at the bottom edge both count as lit here. The recorder flags a hand-off whose human stretch had the indicator lit.

skyvern.ids.evidence: agent-detector's catalogue: Skyvern puts a unique_id attribute on the elements it reads; agent-detector counts it as weaker evidence than its overlay.
skyvern.ids.text: Skyvern's marks were on the page {span}
skyvern.ids.detail: Skyvern's element IDs were on the page {span}.
